claims.claim: RA-MPPI estimates CVaR by brute-force Monte Carlo: for each of M=1024 nominal trajectories it simulates N=300 additional disturbed rollouts, i.e. 3.072e5 trajectories per control step, requiring an RTX 3090 to hold 44.3 Hz. Explicit risk reshaping of the rollout cost distribution is therefore compute-prohibitive in a CPU, K<=256 regime.
claims.quantitative: 3.072e5 rollouts/step at 44.3 Hz on RTX 3090 (M=1024, N=300)
claims.setting: Custom track sim + 1/28-scale race car with Optitrack

claims.claim: Reshaping the tail of the rollout cost distribution before the MPPI softmax (via CVaR of disturbed rollouts) cuts collisions dramatically at essentially unchanged task performance: 80% fewer collisions in sim, 55.7% fewer on hardware (9.0 vs 20.3 collisions/lap) with ~same lap time (7.38 s vs 7.11 s). This is the mechanistic sibling of FPL's bounded atoms compressing cost tails, achieved instead by explicit uncertainty sampling.
claims.quantitative: sim: 80% fewer collisions; hardware: 9.0 vs 20.3 collisions/lap, lap time 7.38 s vs 7.11 s
claims.setting: Aggressive driving in cluttered track, sim + 1/28-scale car

objective_representation: risk (CVaR over Monte Carlo disturbed rollouts)

claims.claim: RMPPI's free-energy growth bound (Lemma 3) decomposes robustness into three terms: distance from a task-constraint threshold, Monte Carlo sampling error, and a tracking-error term scaled by the Lipschitz constants of the terminal and running costs (L_phi, L_q). Bounded, saturating cost atoms (as in FPL) directly shrink these Lipschitz factors, giving a formal pathway by which cost-representation choice alone tightens the robustness bound.

RMPPI (augmented importance sampling propagating nominal + real systems with a feedback tracker inside the sampled rollouts) outperforms both MPPI and Tube-MPPI, operating nearer dynamic limits: sim lap 29.05+-0.96 s at up to 8.84 m/s vs 30.16-30.48 s / ~5.7 m/s for baselines; AutoRally hardware sustains 0.84 rad max slip vs 0.63 (MPPI) at comparable lap times. The cost is an architectural one: a tracking controller (iLQG or CCM) and GPU-scale sampling; the CCM variant was not real-time on CPU.
claims.quantitative: sim: 29.05+-0.96 s vs 30.16-30.48 s laps; hardware: 31.07+-0.33 s, max slip 0.84 vs 0.63 rad
claims.setting: AutoRally 1/5-scale off-road vehicle, sim + hardware, 15 laps each

claims.claim: Tube-MPPI's open-loop nominal-state propagation makes it entirely reliant on the tracking controller; when tracking fails the nominal and actual states diverge and the whole scheme fails, which is why RMPPI re-couples them. Architectural robustness mechanisms carry their own fragility.

objective_representation: linear (quadratic + threshold costs; robustness via architecture, not cost shaping)

claims.claim: The information-theoretic MPPI derivation (free-energy lower bound + KL matching to the optimal Gibbs distribution) places no smoothness or boundedness requirement on the cost: the softmax-weighted update w(V) ~ exp(-S(V)/lambda) accepts arbitrary, even discontinuous, cost functions, and temperature lambda alone controls the peakedness/exploration trade-off. This is the exact pathway FPL's S=-log(u) feeds into, and it is cost-agnostic by construction.
claims.setting: Theory (T-RO, canonical, replicated by essentially every MPPI follow-up)

claims.claim: Across 1,700+ laps (~100 km) on the AutoRally platform at 6/8.5/11 m/s targets, IT-MPC completed 100-lap runs in 17 of 24 scenarios and generally beat CEM-MPC, especially at aggressive speeds, using ~1200 samples of 2.5 s horizons at 40 Hz on an onboard GTX-750ti (~4.8M dynamics queries/s). The canonical baseline regime is GPU-scale sampling, roughly 5x the program's K budget.
claims.quantitative: 17/24 scenarios completed 100 laps; 1200 samples at 40 Hz
claims.setting: AutoRally 1/5-scale vehicle, dirt track, two dynamics models

claims.claim: On a Unitree-class quadruped in simulation, sampling parameterization alone flips task success: cubic-spline sampling with 4 knots achieves 100% success on flat walking, stair climbing, and box traversal, while per-timestep independent Gaussian sampling (the repo's warm-started fixed-Gaussian regime) gets 60% on flat ground and 0% on stairs; Bezier-cp4 also fails stairs at 0%. On contact-rich legged tasks the sampling structure, not the cost, can be the binding constraint.
claims.quantitative: CubicSpline-k4: 100/100/100% vs Normal: 60% flat, 0% stairs; Normal 1358 vs 444 steps to goal on flat

claims.claim: Structured (spline) sampling simultaneously improves sample efficiency, control smoothness, and robustness, with moderate dimensionality (k=4) beating both unstructured noise and higher-dimensional parameterizations (k=8: 80% on box traversal) — a low-cost, untried alternative to the six sampling mechanisms that failed in-repo.
claims.quantitative: CubicSpline-k8 80% vs k4 100% on box traversal

claims.claim: Reformulating the MPPI cost as S~(V)=S(V)+lambda*log(p(V)/q_s(V)) lets arbitrary proposal mixtures (samples from ancillary controllers plus Gaussian samples) enter the estimator with importance weights that depend only on the task cost — a clean, unbiased mechanism for injecting external policy proposals (including a learned student/teacher policy) into MPPI's sample set at negligible cost.

With informed proposals, tiny sample budgets suffice: at K=50 Biased-MPPI had 0 collisions in two-vessel crossing where standard MPPI had 4 at K=50 and still 7 at K=2000; four-agent canal navigation 40/50 successes with 0 collisions at K=50 vs 34/50 with 16 collisions; real Jackal at K=300 had 0 collisions vs 6 for standard MPPI. Proposal quality beats raw sample count, well inside the program's K<=256 CPU regime.
claims.quantitative: K=50: 0 vs 4 collisions (and vs 7 at K=2000); Jackal K=300: 0 vs 6 collisions
claims.setting: Quanser pendulum sim, autonomous vessels sim, Clearpath Jackal hardware

ref: Robust Sampling Based Model Predictive Control with Sparse Objective Information (Williams et al., RSS 2018)

claims.claim: Sparse weighted-indicator costs are easy to specify, interpretable, and act like soft-hard constraints, but make warm-started MPPI brittle under disturbances: when a disturbance pushes the warm-start into a region where indicator terms give zero gradient signal, the sampling distribution cannot recover and the optimizer gets stuck or diverges. Pure indicator (zero-slope) cost representations therefore need an external robustness mechanism — precisely the failure mode FPL's clipped ramps (bounded but sloped inside the band) are shaped to avoid.

An interpretable sparse-indicator spec plus a robustness mechanism (tube with iLQG ancillary tracker and nominal-state accept/reject) approaches or exceeds an extensively hand-tuned dense cost: racing sim Tube-MPPI reached a 9 m/s max target with 9.39+-0.76 s laps vs Tuned-MPPI's 8 m/s / 8.33+-1.05 s, while naive MPPI under the same disturbances collapsed to 5 m/s / 11.87 s. Same shape of claim as FPL's Pareto-dominance over tuned linear weights, achieved architecturally rather than by cost shaping.
claims.quantitative: Tube: 9.39+-0.76 s @ 9 m/s target; Tuned: 8.33+-1.05 s @ 8 m/s; Disturbance-MPPI: 11.87+-0.47 s @ 5 m/s
claims.setting: Gazebo 1/5-scale racing sim with learned hybrid physics-NN model (model error as disturbance source)

claims.claim: On hardware (AutoRally, 12 laps at 9 m/s target, ~2 km) Tube-MPPI held mean nominal-actual state divergence to 14 cm (max 47 cm); in 100-trial helicopter landing, Tube-MPPI eliminated the catastrophic outliers Disturbance-MPPI produced (Tube distance 0.69+-0.15 vs MPPI-large-noise 0.77+-0.25 with tail misses). Compute: 1200 2-s samples at 50 Hz on GPU, iLQG ancillary on a separate CPU thread at 100 Hz.
claims.quantitative: mean divergence 14 cm, max 47 cm; landing distance 0.69+-0.15 vs 0.77+-0.25 with outliers removed
claims.setting: AutoRally hardware + simulated helicopter landing (100 random trials)
claims.where: Tables I, III; Secs. V-B, V-D

objective_representation: other (weighted sparse indicator functions, quasi-logical soft constraints)

claims.claim: RC-MPPI adapts conservatism online from a filtered prediction-execution residual via three coupled mechanisms (constraint tightening, barrier-weight scaling, temperature relaxation), lifting success under severe unmodeled mismatch from 0.64 to 0.94 (point mass with 0.9 s actuator lag) and 0.56 to 0.96 (2R manipulator with inertial error, servo lag, saturation), at claimed zero overhead over standard MPPI. A cheap online-adaptation alternative to a fixed robust spec — but it modifies the controller, not the cost representation, and needs a residual signal.
claims.setting: LTI point mass (K=2048, T=40) and planar 2R manipulator (K=1024, T=35), simulation only

claims.claim: Theory: model-mismatch-induced distortion of MPPI's softmax weights scales as 2*C_Delta*s_bar/beta, where C_Delta is the cost's sensitivity to state error — so raising temperature or capping cost sensitivity provably limits ranking distortion under mismatch. Bounded clipped-ramp atoms cap C_Delta by construction, offering a mechanistic account of why FPL specs degrade gracefully under model error.

MPPI, policy-gradient RL, and diffusion-model sampling are unified as gradient ascent on a (Gaussian-smoothed) Gibbs energy: policy gradient reduces to MPPI under an exponential transformation of rewards, and diffusion reverse sampling follows the same update rule. Purely theoretical, no experiments — but it grounds the H-B design in which an MPPI teacher and an RL student sharing one (FPL) objective are ascending the same smoothed landscape, so distillation should not fight the student's own reward gradient.

The PI-MPC-as-inference survey (MPPI, CEM, GMM/Stein variational, Tsallis-divergence generalizations) treats the cost purely as an arbitrary J inside exp(-J/lambda); it contains no prior work on bounded/normalized fulfillment composition, exponentiated-utility bounds, or formal risk-measure cost transforms in the Boltzmann weighting — the FPL cost-representation slot appears genuinely unoccupied in this family.
claims.setting: Survey/tutorial of the sampling-based MPC family

claims.claim: Robustness to model mismatch is not treated as a design axis anywhere in the surveyed PI-MPC framework; open problems are a-priori sample complexity, exponential sample growth with action dimension, and the absence of formal stability guarantees. The mismatch-robustness question the in-repo benchmark answers is an acknowledged blind spot of the field's own self-description.

Sampling control perturbations from a normal-log-normal mixture yields wider state-space coverage with >30% less injected variance than vanilla Gaussian MPPI, converting into robustness gains without touching cost or architecture: 96% vs 84% success in 1.5 m-spaced clutter, 1 vs 7 collisions in dense forest, shorter and lower-variance paths (72.64+-0.80 m vs 76.12+-3.31 m).
claims.quantitative: 96% vs 84% success; 1 vs 7 collisions; >30% variance reduction
claims.setting: Cartpole sim + Clearpath Jackal with VLP-16 LiDAR, cluttered forests and indoor, K=2500 on GTX 1660 Ti at 50 Hz

claims.claim: Low-pass Butterworth filtering of the sampled perturbations (uniform-energy passband, unlike 1/f colored noise which biases toward the lowest frequencies) improves MPPI across morphologies on a SINGLE CPU CORE at N=100-256 in MuJoCo: +24% average over MPPI variants on Hopper/Ant/HalfCheetah (10% over the best baseline, ColoredMPPI), +24% (Unitree Go2) and +41% (MAB Silver Badger) over Dial-MPC for quadruped trot with ColoredMPPI ~2x worse, and wins on real F1TENTH at N=10 and N=50, with +2.4% overhead. Directly demonstrates that CPU-budget, K<=256, morphology-spanning MPPI is real-time viable and still improvable via noise shaping.
claims.quantitative: +24% Gym avg, +24%/+41% quadrupeds, F1TENTH best at N=10/50; Intel i5-12500H single core, N=100-256, H=15-16
claims.setting: MuJoCo Gymnasium (Hopper/Ant/HalfCheetah), Unitree Go2 + MAB Silver Badger sim, real F1TENTH oval

claims.claim: Spectra of RL-trained expert policies concentrate around ~2 Hz and match low-pass-filtered noise better than 1/f colored noise — the specific frequency shaping matters, and the colored-noise/iCEM family (which failed in-repo) is the wrong shaping, consistent with the repo's negative result.
claims.quantitative: ColoredMPPI ~2x worse than LP variant on quadrupeds
claims.setting: Spectral analysis of RL policies vs noise processes

claims.claim: The generalized importance-sampling derivation (likelihood ratio between diffusion processes with different drift AND covariance) legitimizes sampling from distributions other than the passive dynamics — the theoretical license behind every biased/adaptive-covariance/structured-noise MPPI variant, including the six that failed in-repo. The theory permits covariance change; it does not predict when it helps.
claims.setting: Theory (Feynman-Kac / path-integral derivation), 2015 preprint whose machinery was absorbed into peer-reviewed successors

claims.claim: Natural system noise is insufficient for exploration: race-car and quadrotor tasks required exploration-variance multipliers of 50-300x over natural noise, with 10-1000 rollouts at 50 Hz, and explicit (non-smoothed) crash/obstacle costs outperformed smooth approximations — early evidence that MPPI tolerates hard cost structure that gradient methods cannot, provided injected variance is large.
claims.quantitative: variance multipliers 50-300x; 10-1000 rollouts at 50 Hz; MPPI < DDP average cost
claims.setting: Race car and quadrotor simulation vs DDP baseline

claims.claim: Diffusion-style dual annealing of sampling covariance (over MPPI iterations and over horizon depth) reduces walk-tracking error 7.9-9.6x vs tuned MPPI variants and 22.7x vs CMA-ES on a full-order Unitree Go2 torque-control task.
claims.quantitative: tracking error 0.024 (DIAL-MPC) vs 0.190/0.230 (MPPI-explore/exploit) vs 0.544 (CMA-ES)
claims.setting: Brax/JAX sim + real Go2, 2048 samples, 20-step horizon, 50 Hz, RTX 4090

claims.claim: Training-free sampling MPC beats a goal-conditioned RL policy by 50% on crate climbing (90% vs 20-30% success for MPPI baselines) and needs fewer reward terms than the RL baseline (6 vs 8).
claims.quantitative: 0.9 success vs 0.2-0.3 (MPPI/CMA-ES); GCRL tracking 4.96x worse
claims.setting: Unitree Go2 sim + hardware jumping with payload; H1 humanoid crate-pushing

claims.claim: The capability level demonstrated (agile jumping, climbing) required 2048 parallel GPU rollouts, an order of magnitude above a K<=256 CPU budget.
claims.quantitative: 2048 samples on RTX 4090, JAX/Brax

claims.claim: Real-time derivative-free predictive control on CPU (1-20 ms planning updates via multithreaded MuJoCo rollouts) is feasible across humanoid standing/recovery, quadruped terrain traversal, and Shadow-Hand cube reorientation with one framework.
claims.quantitative: 1-20 ms per planning iteration on 72-core Xeon and Apple M1 Pro
claims.setting: MJPC: 27-DoF humanoid, Unitree A1, Shadow Hand, MuJoCo CPU

claims.claim: Trivial random search over spline-parameterized controls (Predictive Sampling: N-1 Gaussian samples around a nominal, keep the best) is competitive with iLQG and gradient descent, but the paper reports no quantitative planner comparison.

Cost specification is per-task hand-tuned weighted norms over residuals (quadratic, cosh, smooth-abs) with an optional exponential risk transform rho(l,R)=(e^{Rl}-1)/R; no bounded/fulfillment-logic composition exists in this canonical framework.

objective_representation: linear (weighted norms of residuals) + risk transform

claims.claim: A single 317M-parameter learned world model with MPPI-style latent planning performs 80 tasks across embodiments and action spaces (zero-padded/masked actions), and one hyperparameter set works across 104 online RL tasks.
claims.quantitative: 80-task agent, ~70.6 normalized score; 104 tasks, single hyperparameter set
claims.setting: DMControl (incl. Dog/Humanoid, up to 38-D actions) + Meta-World; RTX 3090

claims.claim: The learned-model route to morphology generality costs 33 GPU-days of training for the 317M agent and uses 512-sample planning over a neural model, incompatible with a training-free CPU MuJoCo stack.
claims.quantitative: 33 GPU-days (317M), 512 samples, horizon 3, 6 iterations

claims.claim: MPPI with K=128 CPU MuJoCo rollouts runs at ~280 Hz average on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 (sim) when seeded by a pretrained RL policy as sampling prior, using 2 spline knots and a 0.02 s horizon.
claims.quantitative: N=128, ~280 Hz, i9-14900KF CPU (rollouts CPU-side via MJPC)
claims.setting: MuJoCo sim, G1 humanoid, asynchronous planning

claims.claim: MPPI as a feedback layer on top of RL cuts lateral drift RMSE from 0.339 m to 0.022 m (15x) vs pure RL under the same command interface, using tiny quadratic cost terms.
claims.quantitative: lateral RMSE 0.339->0.022 m; lateral velocity RMSE 0.046->0.021 m/s
claims.setting: G1 straight-walk and squat tasks, sim only

claims.claim: The direction of coupling is RL-into-MPPI (policy as sampling prior), the reverse of MPPI-as-teacher; a pretrained RL policy was required, not produced.

Sampling parameterization dominates MPPI performance on legged robots: cubic-spline knots (k=4) achieve 100% success on flat walking, stairs, and box traversal where unstructured per-timestep Gaussian sampling scores 60%, 0%, and 0% respectively under identical costs.
claims.quantitative: stairs: cubic k=4 100% vs baseline 0%; flat: 444 vs 1358 steps to goal

claims.claim: Over-parameterization hurts: k=8 knots degraded box-traversal robustness to 80% vs 100% at k=4, supporting low-dimensional smooth sampling as the design principle.
claims.quantitative: k=8: 80% vs k=4: 100% on box traversal

claims.claim: Real-world whole-body MPPI on a Unitree Go1 works with only 30-50 CPU MuJoCo rollouts at 100 Hz (cubic splines, 4 knots, 0.4 s horizon), handling walking, climbing obstacles at robot height (0.24 m), and box pushing with one controller and no offline training.
claims.quantitative: 30-50 samples, 100 Hz, i9-12900KS; box pushing 9/10 forward, 6/10 lateral

claims.claim: Loco-manipulation emerges from adding an L1 box-position term to a tracking cost, i.e. task recomposition by cost editing rather than retraining.

Reference-free MPPI with jointly-sampled cubic Hermite splines (position and velocity control points) plus annealing discovers emergent gaits (walk, trot, gallop, jump, backflip, handstand) from cost objectives alone, with 30 samples on a real Go2 and 60-70 samples on a 37-DoF G1 in sim, all real-time on standard CPU.
claims.quantitative: 30 samples (quadruped) vs 2048-4096 for GPU competitors; 60-70 (humanoid)
claims.setting: real Go2, sim G1, CPU only

claims.claim: The same framework transfers quadruped-to-humanoid without algorithmic modification or retuning of the sampler, the closest published morphology-generality claim for pure sampling MPC.
Hermite splines beat cubic and quadratic spline sampling in trajectory cost and success rate in ablation, replicating (with a third group) the structured-sampling finding.

objective_representation: linear (modular: base tracking, joint regularization, contact penalties, terminal displacement)

claims.claim: MPPI (120 rollouts, CPU) plus a learned ensemble value function solves humanoid getup in ~24 CPU core-hours vs ~128 for policy-gradient methods, and in-hand reorientation in ~1 CPU-hour vs ~500 for model-free RL: 5-500x sample/compute efficiency from planning-accelerated value learning.
claims.quantitative: 24 vs 128 core-hours (humanoid); 1 vs 500 CPU-hours (hand)
claims.setting: MuJoCo humanoid + dexterous hand, 120/80 MPPI rollouts, H=64

claims.claim: A terminal value function substitutes for planning horizon: shorter-horizon MPC with learned V matches longer-horizon value-free MPC, and trajectory optimization stabilizes value learning (the mechanism H-B relies on, demonstrated in 2018).
claims.quantitative: N-step targets accelerate convergence (Fig. 4a)

claims.claim: The sampling-MPC update is a Monte Carlo estimate of score ascent on a noised target distribution, so SPC can supervise flow-matching policy training without demonstrations; the resulting GPC policies match or beat PPO with equivalent data on 7 systems up to 29 DoF.
claims.quantitative: GPC/GPC+ on par or better than PPO; training 30 s (pendulum) to 113 min (humanoid) on RTX 4070
claims.setting: MuJoCo MJX/JAX, sim only: pendulum to humanoid standup

claims.claim: Pure distillation of the sampling-MPC teacher fails on the hardest task (humanoid standup); only GPC+, which keeps the policy in the loop seeding SPC at deployment, remains effective, and warm-starting is critical (without it actions jitter between modes).
claims.quantitative: basic GPC fails reliably on humanoid standup; GPC+ succeeds

claims.claim: Teacher cost and student objective are linked only through sampled (state,action) data, not a shared spec; the student has no reward, it is a generative model of teacher actions.

The MPPI softmax mean update is the closed-form global optimum of a concave KL objective at fixed covariance, and the framework accepts arbitrary cost functions including discontinuous penalties and indicator functions - so bounded [0,1] fulfillment values are formally admissible inputs to the Boltzmann weighting.
claims.setting: tutorial/survey of PI-MPC (MPPI, CEM, VI-MPC, SVGD, diffusion samplers)

claims.claim: The survey provides no taxonomy of cost shaping and explicitly does not discuss multi-objective composition; constraint handling is limited to clamping, penalties, projection, or SVGD - confirming that bounded fulfillment-logic cost composition in sampling MPC is unmapped territory in the field's own self-survey.

Imitate-then-finetune from an MPC expert (DAgger then RL) converges in ~2000 iterations vs ~4000 for RL from scratch on quadruped locomotion - a 2x iteration speedup, the concrete effect-size anchor for the MPC-teacher hypothesis.
claims.quantitative: ~2000 vs ~4000 iterations; inference 15.4 ms (MPC) -> 1 ms (policy)
claims.setting: RaiSim sim + Mini Cheetah hardware; DDP-based MPC expert

claims.claim: The RL fine-tuning reward is deliberately different from the MPC cost (simple velocity-tracking/torque reward, optionally with contact biasing, vs the MPC's state-tracking cost), and the pipeline still works and surpasses the teacher (90% vs 0% success on 7.5 cm obstacles).
claims.quantitative: 90% vs 0% MPC success on 7.5 cm obstacles

claims.claim: MPC pre-training prevents jerky asymmetric gaits and reduces reward engineering vs pure RL, i.e. the teacher's main gift is a behavior basin, not the cost function itself.

objective_representation: linear (MPC tracking cost; separate RL reward)

claims.claim: Butterworth low-pass filtering of sampled MPPI perturbations (uniform passband, unlike colored noise's 1/f damping) improves over vanilla MPPI, SMPPI, SCP-MPPI, and ColoredMPPI across Gymnasium (~10%, up to 26-36% vs SMPPI/SCP-MPPI), quadruped trot sim (24-41% over a DIAL-MPC baseline), and real F1TENTH racing, at negligible compute overhead.
claims.quantitative: +10% Gymnasium avg; 24-41% over DIAL-MPC baseline (quadruped); +2.4% overhead
claims.setting: Hopper/Ant/HalfCheetah, Go2 + Silver Badger sim, real F1TENTH; N=10 and N=50 rollouts

claims.claim: Gains hold at N=10 and N=50 rollouts with only two interpretable parameters (cutoff frequency, filter order), so a morphology-spanning sampler improvement exists inside the CPU K<=256 budget - and it is distinct from the colored-noise mechanism the in-repo negative tested.
claims.quantitative: N=10 and N=50 both best-in-class on F1TENTH

morphologies: Unitree Go2 + MAB Silver Badger quadrupeds (sim)

claims.claim: The MPPI softmax weighting is derived as the exact free-energy/KL-optimal tilted distribution q*(V) ∝ exp(-S/λ)p(V); the algorithm is the KL projection of this optimum onto Gaussians, and the derivation places no smoothness, convexity, or boundedness requirements on the state cost — any transform (including FPL's S=-log(u)) is admissible without altering optimality.
claims.setting: Theory + AutoRally 1/5-scale vehicle, 1200 samples, GTX-750ti, 40 Hz

claims.claim: Derivative-free handling of discontinuous costs and constraint clamping pushed into dynamics enables aggressive dirt-track driving at 40-60 Hz, outperforming a cross-entropy MPC baseline over 1700+ laps / 100+ km.
claims.quantitative: 1200 rollouts at 40 Hz; ~4.8M dynamics queries/s; 1700+ laps of validation

claims.claim: The cost-to-weight transform is a free design axis: replacing exp with the deformed exponential exp_q interpolates continuously between MPPI (q→1) and CEM's top-elite indicator (q→∞), with an explicit absolute-risk-aversion interpretation — the closest published theoretical frame for FPL's log-power-mean cost transform.

Tsallis-transformed weighting lowers cost mean and especially variance versus both MPPI and CEM across five morphologies at only N=64 samples, showing weight-transform design alone yields robustness gains without touching the sampler.
claims.quantitative: Variance reduction 60-85% on navigation/manipulation; humanoid mean cost 112% better vs MPPI (Table IV); N=64 rollouts
claims.setting: Planar nav, quadcopter, 7-DOF Franka, Ant, 21-DOF humanoid; UG/GM/SVGD policies

claims.claim: Sampling with altered covariance is only valid with a likelihood-ratio correction that enters as an additional running cost (a term penalizing over-aggressive exploration plus Girsanov terms); adaptive-covariance schemes omitting it bias the estimator — a candidate post-mortem for the program's failed adaptive-covariance sampler.

Large exploration-variance inflation (nu = 50-1500x natural noise) is necessary for MPPI to solve cart-pole swing-up and beat DDP on aggressive racing — fixed but well-scaled covariance, not adaptation, is what matters.
claims.quantitative: Cart-pole unsolvable without inflation (cost ~2000); solved with nu=1500 at 1000 samples; race car needs nu 50-300x
claims.setting: Cart-pole, race car, quadrotor obstacle field; 10-1000 rollouts, GPU, 50 Hz

claims.claim: MPPI provably converges at least linearly on quadratic objectives, and the rate depends explicitly on sampling covariance; the convergence-optimal covariance schedule exists in closed form but requires the cost Hessian.
claims.setting: Theory: time-varying LQR, extended to nonlinear

claims.claim: Optimal covariance design (CoVO-MPC) beats standard MPPI by 43-54% on quadrotor agile control — proof that fixed isotropic Gaussians are suboptimal in principle, yet the required Hessian information is unavailable in a derivative-free CPU MuJoCo pipeline, rationalizing why fixed Gaussians are the practical optimum at K<=256.
claims.quantitative: 43-54% cost improvement over MPPI, sim and real quadrotor

claims.claim: Standard MPPI's failure mode under disturbance is the importance sampler staying anchored to an open-loop nominal trajectory, causing unbounded free-energy jumps when the real state diverges; free-energy growth is bounded jointly by constraint slack, tracking-controller contraction rate, and Monte-Carlo sampling error.

RMPPI's augmented nominal/real-state importance sampling permits more aggressive operation than MPPI or Tube-MPPI under disturbances without violating free-energy bounds — robustness under mismatch requires either architectural augmentation or (hypothesis for FPL) bounded costs that cap weight ratios.
claims.quantitative: Target speed 9 m/s vs 7 m/s for MPPI/Tube-MPPI in sim; hardware laps 31.07±0.33 s at higher max slip (0.84 rad); ~15 laps per controller
claims.setting: AutoRally Gazebo sim + 1/5-scale hardware, iLQG and CCM tracking controllers, GPU

claims.claim: Diffusion-style dual-loop annealing of sampling covariance (exponential decay across outer iterations, larger variance for later horizon steps) reduces quadruped torque-level tracking error vs fixed-covariance MPPI by up to 13.4x and beats RL by 50% on climbing — the strongest published counterexample to 'fixed-Gaussian MPPI is unbeatable', but at 2048 samples x multiple anneal iterations on an RTX 4090 (JAX/Brax), far outside a K<=256 CPU budget.
claims.quantitative: Walk tracking 0.024 vs 0.190-0.230 (MPPI explore/exploit), 13.4x aggregate; climbing success 0.9 vs 0.2-0.3; 2048 samples, 50 Hz, RTX 4090
claims.setting: Unitree Go2-class quadruped, Brax/JAX GPU, sim + hardware
claims.where: Eqs. 5-7, Prop. 1, Tables I, III, Fig. 4

claims.claim: Under 2 kg mass-model mismatch, annealed sampling retains 92-126% better performance than fixed-covariance MPPI — sampler design, not only cost design, can buy mismatch robustness given GPU-scale budgets.
claims.quantitative: Walking error 0.188 vs 0.361; jumping reward 0.610 vs 0.270 under 2 kg mismatch

claims.claim: Non-differentiable min/max-composed STL robustness costs are used directly (unsmoothed) inside a path-integral optimizer that anneals both covariance and temperature toward the deterministic limit — the closest published prior art to logic-structured costs in MPPI and mandatory citation for FPL novelty claims.

On a nested STL problem with a kinematic car (horizon 50), annealed path integral converges in 25 s while MIP and gradient methods exceed a 1-hour timeout and only CMA-ES also solves it (80 s) — sampling handles logic-composed nonsmooth landscapes where model-based smoothing solvers fail, but needed up to 81k samples over 40 iterations.
claims.quantitative: PI 25.07 s vs CMA-ES 79.82 s; MIP/GRAD/SGRAD >3600 s; M up to 81,650 samples, J=40 iterations
claims.setting: Scalar integrator, 2D double integrator, kinematic single-track vehicle; CPU

claims.claim: A single Stein-variational guide particle that moves only MPPI's nominal sequence toward a mode (preserving the closed-form update) cuts collision rate from 13.6% to 4.0% (sim) and 55.6% to 15.4% (real) at 11 ms on CPU — mode-seeking guidance can beat vanilla MPPI cheaply when it augments rather than replaces the estimator, unlike the program's failed GMM+SUS resampling.
claims.quantitative: Collision rate 4.0% vs 13.6% (sim), 15.4% vs 55.6% (real); path-tracking cost 0.20 vs 1.36; 11.0 ms avg on Core i9 CPU; Kg=1 guide particle
claims.setting: 1/10-scale vehicle, sim + real, 2k-8k MPPI samples, CPU only
claims.where: Eqs. 9, 12-13; Sec. IV-B, V-B/V-C, Tables I-II

claims.claim: The MPC-as-inference survey's design taxonomy (prior design, posterior family, temperature, constraints, scalability, theory) contains no dedicated treatment of cost-function design or pre-Boltzmann cost transformation — the survey explicitly assumes costs are given — confirming FPL occupies an unclaimed design axis.

The survey's theory section reports only linear convergence for infinite-sample quadratic costs and notes finite-sample convergence and required-sample estimation remain open, with no stability analysis for general nonlinear MPPI — the theoretical basis for beating (or certifying) warm-started MPPI is thin.

Closing the temperature loop with Shannon entropy of importance weights (cool aggressively when weights diffuse, hold when concentrated; lambda_{j+1}=Gamma(H)lambda_j) provably drives lambda to 0 eliminating MPPI bias, with a critical entropy threshold guarding against premature weight collapse ('glassification').

On nonsmooth STL motion-planning tasks (2D point mass, N=3000 rollouts), entropy-feedback cooling converges up to 4.1x faster than fixed schedules and lifts success on the hardest corridor task from 16% to 22% — temperature adaptation helps in iteration-rich deterministic planning, a regime distinct from the warm-started receding-horizon loop.
claims.quantitative: 13 vs 48 iterations (Task B); up to 4.14x compute reduction; success 22% vs 16% (Task C); 100 trials/task

claims.claim: Adapting conservatism online from prediction-execution residuals (constraint tightening m=L_h(c_r*s+c_0), penalty scaling alpha=alpha_0(1+gamma*s), exploration contraction plus temperature relaxation) lifts success under actuator-lag mismatch from 0.64 to 0.94 (LTI point mass) and 0.56 to 0.96 (2R manipulator) vs vanilla MPPI — evidence that residual-adaptive mechanisms beat a fixed configuration under mismatch, though only on toy systems.
claims.quantitative: Success 0.64→0.94 and 0.56→0.96; violation steps 4.16→0.62 and 3.08→0.10; K=2048/1024 rollouts, 50 paired-seed trials
claims.setting: LTI point mass (T=40) and planar 2R manipulator (T=35) with servo lag, saturation, inertial errors

claims.claim: Model-plant mismatch perturbs MPPI importance weights by at most 2*C_a*s/beta, so raising temperature when residuals grow provably reduces overcommitment to unreliable cost rankings — a weighting-side (not sampler-side) robustness mechanism consistent with the program's cost-side-wins pattern.
claims.quantitative: Weight L1 perturbation bound 2*C_a*s̄/β

claims.claim: For spatially varying unknown disturbance covariance, a cell-wise recursive estimator with reversible spatial-diffusion smoothing yields an adaptive stability certificate that becomes strictly tighter than ANY fixed covariance choice after a computable finite crossover time (payoff theorem) — adaptivity provably wins, but only asymptotically and so far only in LTI-style simulation with very long horizons (T=8000).
claims.quantitative: Estimation error bound C1/sqrt(k) + smoothing bias + Cv*eps_v*T; crossover time k* <= T
claims.setting: Theory + grid-cell simulation, 19-page 2026 preprint, companion to 2607.04006
claims.where: Theorem 2 / Sec. IV-D, Eq. 9, Lemma 1, Sec. V

claims.claim: FPL defines fulfillment as bounded [0,1] values composed by weighted power means (p from -inf min to +inf max), with negation 1-u, disjunction via De Morgan, and soft-lexicographic priority via offset operator u([phi]_delta)=(u(phi)+max(delta,0))/(1+delta).

FQ-values are defined as (1-gamma)*Q, i.e. discount-normalized Q-values in [0,1]; the paper's Balanced Policy Gradient (DDPG extension) regularizes the critic with observed discounted fulfillment sums to counter overestimation bias.
claims.quantitative: critic Q-error 0.627 -> 0.146 with alpha_FV=0.75 on Hopper at 38k steps

claims.claim: BPG with an FPL spec is markedly more sample-efficient than strong RL baselines: LunarLander 20k steps to reward 200 vs 128k (DDPG) and 36k (CrossQ); Hopper 27.4k steps to 2000 vs 66.6k (CrossQ); with FPL the Hopper reward-hacking mode (standing still for ~1000 reward) is eliminated (FPL fulfillment 3.8e-5 for it), yielding 2288 vs 750 average reward at 48k steps over 10 seeds.
claims.quantitative: up to ~5x sample-efficiency vs SAC; 84% fewer steps vs DDPG on LunarLander; FPL spec score 0.625 vs 0.194 without
claims.setting: Pendulum, Reacher, Hopper, LunarLander (+ preliminary HalfCheetah/Walker2d/Ant)

claims.claim: The FPL paper contains no mention of MPC, MPPI, or planning; it acknowledges lower asymptotic performance of BPG and sensitivity to FQ overestimation as limitations.

STL space-robustness costs (raw, non-smoothed min/max semantics) are optimized by a deterministic path-integral method that anneals covariance and temperature by factor nu over J iterations, with proven convergence to the deterministic optimum as M,J -> inf; sampling handles the non-differentiability so no smooth robustness approximation is needed.

On a 5D kinematic-vehicle STL benchmark the path-integral solver finds satisfying trajectories in 25s on a laptop CPU (AMD Ryzen 5 PRO 7540U, no GPU) where MIP (Gurobi), gradient SLSQP, and smoothed-robustness SLSQP all time out beyond 3600s; on simpler problems it is near-optimal (cost -2.98 vs MIP -3.0) in 24ms.

claims.setting: scalar integrator, 4D motion planning, 5D single-track vehicle

claims.claim: Achieving deterministic STL optimization required M up to 81,650 samples times J=40 iterations on the hardest problem, far beyond a K<=256 per-step MPPI budget.
claims.quantitative: 3.3M total rollouts for Problem III
claims.setting: offline trajectory optimization, not receding horizon

claims.claim: STL-SVPIO transports a mutually repulsive swarm of only 10 control particles via Stein variational gradient descent using exact STL robustness gradients (LogSumExp-smoothed, STLCG++ autodiff through JAX/MJX differentiable simulation), solving nested long-horizon STL tasks.
claims.quantitative: 10 particles vs 1024-2048 for the DPI baseline
claims.setting: 2D point mass, multi-agent, 7-DoF Franka (MuJoCo MJX), Half-Cheetah backflip

claims.claim: Plain MPPI with handcrafted costs fails on sparse, long-horizon temporally nested STL objectives: on reach-avoid MPPI attains robustness 0.005 vs STL-SVPIO 0.108, and MPPI fails entirely on multi-agent synchronization; the stated mechanism is exponential decay of importance weights under sparse costs and mode collapse.

claims.quantitative: 19-593s per solve on RTX A6000

claims.claim: AGM robustness replaces min/max STL semantics with normalized mean-based aggregation bounded in [-1,1]: conjunction/always use a geometric mean of (1+eta) terms, disjunction/eventually use an arithmetic mean of positive parts, rewarding both how robustly and how often subformulae hold, while remaining sound (sign agrees with satisfaction).

Policies optimized with AGM robustness (proximal stochastic gradient ascent) survive Gaussian perturbations better than those optimized with smooth min/max approximations at equal nominal scores: ~59% vs ~42% satisfaction under noise.
claims.quantitative: 59% vs 42% satisfaction under Gaussian noise

claims.claim: Adding a CVaR tail-risk penalty to MPPI rollout costs (estimated by N=300 stochastic inner rollouts per each of M=1024 nominal trajectories) cuts collisions by ~80% in simulation and 55.7% on a physical 1/28-scale race car at essentially unchanged lap time (7.38s vs 7.11s).

claims.quantitative: 3.072e5 rollouts/step; 27.8-81.6 Hz on GPU

claims.claim: This paper establishes tail-of-cost-distribution reshaping as a sufficient explanation for robustness gains in MPPI, which is a rival hypothesis to FPL's semantic explanation: bounded [0,1] atoms also compress cost tails before the softmax, so the in-repo FPL Pareto win needs an ablation against clipped/saturated linear costs to rule this out.

Priority-ordered STL specifications are already optimized inside standard MPPI: a rank-preserving reward sum_j(a*2^(N-j+1)*step(rho_j) + rho_j/N) encodes hard lexicographic ordering over STL rules, evaluated exactly per rollout with no differentiability requirement, under multimodal uncertainty handled by scenario trees plus CVaR over scenario losses.
claims.setting: highway cut-in and unsignalized intersection, kinematic bicycle

claims.claim: The MPPI sample budget is only V=220-240 rollouts at 0.77-2.49 ms per planning step (CUDA-parallelized on RTX 5060; kinematic bicycle dynamics), i.e. logic-structured MPPI works at rollout counts comparable to the program's K<=256 - though with trivial dynamics, not full physics.

RRT-eta independently adopts FPL: it maps AGM robustness intervals to bounded fulfillment values f_i=(eta_upper+eta_lower+2)/4 in [0,1] and composes them with FPL power means (p -> -inf conjunctive to p -> +inf disjunctive), explicitly citing FPL as enabling prioritization of less-fulfilled objectives, with aggregation weights taken from power-mean derivatives.
claims.setting: sampling-based motion planning (offline RRT), not MPC

claims.claim: Incremental robustness monitoring reduces per-observation STL evaluation from O(|s|*|phi|) to O(|phi|), cutting spec-evaluation overhead from thousands to hundreds of operations per trajectory - directly transferable to keeping FPL atom evaluation cheap inside CPU MPPI rollouts.
claims.quantitative: O(|s|) speedup; ~10x fewer ops for typical |s|=20-50

claims.claim: RRT-eta is an offline planner with no receding-horizon or MPC component, so FPL-composed costs inside sampling MPC remains unoccupied territory even after this adoption.

Lexicographic priorities over conflicting STL specs are collapsed into one scalar by discretizing each violation metric into integer levels and bit-shifting: s(y)=sum c_i(y)*2^(B_i), with a proven equivalence between lexicographic order and scalar order; solved by their deterministic MPPI with the quadratic input-cost requirement eliminated (R(beta)=beta*lambda*Sigma^-1 -> 0) and a cosine annealing schedule.
claims.setting: IEEE OJ-ITS (listed), CommonRoad driving benchmarks, CPU (Threadripper PRO 5975WX)

claims.quantitative: 11 robustness definitions compared

claims.claim: The authors flag that nested min/max robustness misdirects learning when sub-formulae have different physical scales and that normalization is manual - the precise documented pain point that bounded [0,1] fulfillment atoms with satisfied bands are designed to eliminate.

D-GMSR builds C1-smooth STL robustness from weighted geometric and power means (p>=1) over squared positive/negative parts, and is the only measure in their comparison that is simultaneously smooth, sound, complete, and free of locality/masking problems (vs D-SR, LSE, D-SSR, AGM) for any epsilon>0 rather than asymptotically.

D-GMSR robustness values are unbounded and unnormalized, depending on raw predicate magnitudes - power-mean aggregation prior art exists here, but the bounded-[0,1]-atom normalization step remains FPL's distinguishing move.

LSE-smoothed robustness (D-SSR, kappa=25) fails to satisfy a simple reach specification due to masking while the mean-based measure converges - concrete evidence that mean-family aggregation is better-behaved than softmin/LSE for spec optimization.
claims.setting: illustrative reach problem; quadrotor (21 nodes/20s); 6-DoF rocket landing with 14 state-triggered constraints

claims.claim: A learned neural dynamics model plus sampling MPC (CMA-ES) directly maximizing STL robustness over predicted trajectories solves Cartpole, Mountain Car, Fetch reach, adaptive cruise control, and parking without reward engineering - the closest existing pipeline shape to an FPL+MPPI teacher, but it has no policy student, no distillation, and no baseline comparisons.

claims.setting: learned model, receding horizon, first action executed

A rule hierarchy of N STL rules is collapsed into one differentiable rank-preserving reward R(rho)=sum(a^(N-i+1)*step(rho_i)+rho_i/N), a>2, with Theorem 1 proving lower rank implies strictly higher reward; sigmoid-relaxed for gradient refinement via STLCG autodiff.

claims.setting: ICRA 2023 (NVIDIA); highway-gym, kinematic bicycle; Threadripper 3975WX + RTX 3090

claims.quantitative: 0.091-0.105 s mean planning time across scenarios

claims.claim: Rank preservation requires exponential weight separation a^(N-i+1), which for bounded rewards compresses lower-priority gradient signal exponentially in N - the failure mode FPL's soft priority offsets (delta in [-1,1], bounded output) are designed to avoid; this is the sharpest published competitor to argue against.

FPL composes bounded [0,1] fulfillment atoms via weighted power means (p interpolating min to max) with priority offsets delta in [-1,1] giving soft lexicographic ordering; demonstrated only with a policy-gradient learner (BPG, a DDPG extension), never in planning or MPC.
FPL-specified BPG reaches reward thresholds far faster than baselines: LunarLander threshold in 20k steps vs 36k (CrossQ) and 128k (DDPG); up to 500% better sample efficiency than SAC.
claims.quantitative: 84% fewer steps vs DDPG, 44% vs CrossQ on LunarLander; 59% reduction vs CrossQ on Hopper; up to 500% vs SAC

claims.claim: One FPL spec generalized across HalfCheetah-v4, Walker2d-v4, Ant-v4 without retuning, and behavior is robust to reasonable variation in power-mean parameters (p chosen as 0 or -1) and seeds, unlike linear weighted rewards.
claims.quantitative: Hopper fulfillment 0.625 with FPL vs 0.194 without

Controllers synthesized by maximizing AGM robustness are more robust to disturbance than those maximizing smooth-approximated traditional robustness: failure rate 41% vs 58% under Gaussian control noise.

AGM interval semantics over partial trajectories give incremental monitoring at O(|s||phi|) vs O(|s|^2|phi|), and the AGM landscape is 'significantly smoother than traditional min-max robustness' though still non-convex.

claims.claim: For nonlinear utility functions the Bellman equation does not decompose (utility does not distribute over immediate plus future returns), and SER (utility of expected return) vs ESR (expected utility of return) yield significantly different optimal policies - directly relevant because MPPI applies the FPL utility per-rollout (ESR-like) while a critic-based RL student estimates expectations (SER-like).

Linear scalarization cannot express many human preferences and puts trade-off authority with engineers via semi-blind weight tuning; monotonically increasing nonlinear utilities retain Pareto-consistency while expressing richer preferences, and non-stationary policies can Pareto-dominate stationary ones under nonlinear utility.

Godel/min conjunction and minimum aggregation are 'single-passing': at most one input receives nonzero derivative, so min-like conjunctions starve all but one subobjective of learning signal; Lukasiewicz aggregation has nonvanishing derivative on only 1/n! of the domain.
claims.quantitative: nonvanishing fraction 1/n! (Lukasiewicz), 1/2^(n-1) (nilpotent)
claims.setting: analytic study of differentiable fuzzy operators + semi-supervised toy experiments

claims.claim: Product/geometric-mean-family operators (product t-norm, log-product, generalized-mean aggregators) have nonvanishing gradients everywhere and are recommended for learning; best learning performance requires operator combinations that no longer satisfy classical logical laws - independent theoretical support for FPL's empirical choice of p=0/-1 over p->-inf, and a mechanism for why hard min-like conjunctions degrade both gradient learners and rank-based samplers.

Reward machines have regular-language expressivity (loops, sequences, conditionals, non-Markovian temporally extended rewards) that a flat memoryless atom composition like FPL cannot express without added automaton state.

Value-based lexicographic RL converges only if the slack tolerance tau is smaller than the minimum Q-value gap, which 'can in general not be determined a priori' - hard lexicographic ordering is intrinsically fragile to tolerance tuning, consonant with the repo's finding that hard lexicographic shields underperform soft priority offsets.

claims.quantitative: ~300x (0.125 ms vs 38 ms); 15x in IFM

claims.claim: The exact H-B pipeline shape (DAgger-imitate a DDP-based MPC expert, then PPO fine-tune) converges in about half the iterations of RL from scratch (~2000 vs ~4000 PPO iterations) while using a minimally constructed reward.
claims.quantitative: ~2000 vs ~4000 iterations to convergence (~2x)

claims.claim: The fine-tuning reward is NOT the MPC's cost: RL uses a separate simple velocity-tracking + regularization (+ optional contact) reward, i.e. teacher objective and student reward are only loosely coupled — no prior work in this pipeline shares a single spec between planner and RL reward.
claims.quantitative: SR/CR rewards ~3-4 terms vs 'ten terms' typical for vanilla RL

claims.claim: The fine-tuned student surpasses its own MPC teacher on robustness: 90% hardware success on 7.5 cm steps vs 0% for MPC and DAgger-only and 60% for vanilla RL, and tracks on slippery terrain where MPC fails outright — pure model-based MPC is not robust to unmodeled terrain contact.
claims.quantitative: 90% vs 0% (MPC/DAgger) vs 60% (RL) on 7.5 cm step; slip tracking err 0.189 vs 0.655 (RL), MPC failed; symmetry PPI 1.798 vs 10.13 (RL)

claims.claim: Mixture-of-experts MPC-Net with a log-partitioned Hamiltonian loss distills multiple ANYmal gaits (trot + static walk) into a single policy at performance similar to single-gait policies, with experts specializing per hybrid contact mode.
claims.quantitative: multi-gait needs 200k vs 100k training iterations for single-gait

claims.claim: Hamiltonian-loss policies are markedly more robust than behavioral-cloning policies trained on the same MPC data: 10.6+/-6.3 s survival on rough terrain vs 2.6+/-1.6 s for BC — how the teacher's objective enters the student loss matters, not just the data.
claims.quantitative: 10.6 s vs 2.6 s survival (~4x)

claims.claim: Canonical cost-sharing-by-construction: iLQG teacher controllers and the CNN student are cast as one constrained optimization (BADMM with KL constraints enforcing p(u|x)=pi_theta(u|o)), so teacher and student provably optimize the same task cost — the strongest existing form of teacher-student objective coupling.

Shared-cost coupling yields extreme real-robot sample efficiency: complete visuomotor skills from 156-288 trials (~15 min robot execution within 3-4 h total), 88.9-96.3% success vs 0-70.4% for pose-estimation baselines.
Requires full state observability at training time (instrumented setup) and quadratic-cost teachers — the shared cost is a smooth linear/quadratic objective, not a logic or satisfaction spec.

Tightest mutual teacher-student loop found: the policy imitates an MPC expert that is itself guided by the policy (policy-seeded MPPI), with an on-policy n-step TD state-value learned jointly; expert imitation replaces TD-MPC2's value-gradient policy update.
claims.setting: ICLR 2025, latent world model, batched GPU MPPI
claims.quantitative: lazy reanalyze cuts reanalysis from 99% to 0.8% of samples at 10-20% overhead

claims.claim: Policy-guided-expert imitation gives ~3-4x better data efficiency than TD-MPC2 on 7 high-dimensional locomotion tasks (90k vs 360k steps-to-solve) with a smaller network (3M vs 5M params), and the distilled network policy alone reaches near-MPC performance, closing the distillation gap TD-MPC2 leaves open.
claims.quantitative: 90k vs 360k steps-to-solve (~4x); near-zero policy-vs-planner gap

claims.claim: MPPI, policy-gradient RL, and diffusion sampling are unified as gradient ascent on a Gibbs measure over one energy E(U) = -J(U) = R(U) = log p(U) — a theoretical bridge for an MPPI teacher and RL student optimizing 'the same' objective.

The equivalence is exact only under an exponential transform: policy gradient must optimize E[exp(R)] (not E[R]) to match MPPI's update — so an RL student trained on a raw FPL fulfillment reward does NOT optimize the identical objective as an MPPI teacher softmaxing exp(-S) with S=-log(u), unless the reward is transformed consistently.

Injecting MPC transitions into the off-policy replay buffer at a fixed ~25% ratio, with the RL task reward completely unchanged and no imitation loss, steers RL into the controller's behavior basin: upright walking instead of scooting (walker) and structured trot instead of chaotic vibration (Go2) under an identical sparse velocity-tracking reward.
claims.quantitative: 25% injection ratio; gait quality 'comparable to reward shaping with twenty-one tuned terms' and to AMP, with better perturbation robustness than AMP

claims.claim: No steps-to-threshold convergence speedup is reported — the benefit claimed is basin/gait selection and reward-engineering reduction, not sample efficiency; late-training basin drift is acknowledged.

morphologies: simulated quadrotor (canyon/forest navigation, 40D laser or 110D image observations)

claims.claim: An adaptive MPC teacher that optimizes its own task cost PLUS lambda*KL(teacher || student) anticipates the learner's distribution while never executing the student during training, giving safer and faster learning than DAgger: under one crash per iteration vs substantial failures for DAgger/coaching, with equal or better final policies.
claims.setting: simulated quadrotor, MPC always in control during training
claims.quantitative: <1 crash/iteration vs 'substantial' failures for DAgger

claims.claim: The student never observes the task cost as a reward — it only regresses MPC action labels (weighted Euclidean loss) on its own observations; the objective coupling lives entirely in the teacher's optimization.

DIAL-MPC's dual-loop diffusion-style annealing (covariance shrinks jointly across N outer annealing iterations and along the horizon, det(Sigma) decaying exponentially in both indices) reduces quadruped tracking error 13.4x versus standard MPPI and beats trained RL policies by 50% on climbing, with no training. This is a pure schedule-side mechanism: the proposal stays Gaussian; only its variance schedule changes.
claims.quantitative: Walk-track error 0.024 vs 0.190 (MPPI-explore) and 0.544 (CMA-ES); crate-climb score 0.9 vs 0.2-0.3; 13.4x tracking-error reduction; +50% vs RL
claims.setting: Torque-level full-order quadruped control, JAX/Brax, RTX 4090, 2048 samples, 20-step horizon, 50 Hz; real Unitree jumping with payload
claims.where: Results tables (walk track / sequential jump / crate climb); Sec. on annealing schedule

claims.claim: No ablation isolates the annealing schedule parameters (beta1, beta2), so how much of the gain survives at K<=256 CPU samples is unknown; the schedule itself costs zero extra rollouts.

RA-MPPI is weight-side: for each of M candidate trajectories it estimates CVaR of the cost under N=300 auxiliary disturbance rollouts and adds it as a penalty before the standard MPPI softmax, cutting collisions 55.7% on real hardware and 80% in simulation at essentially unchanged lap time.
claims.quantitative: Real: 9.0 vs 20.3 collisions/lap at 7.38s vs 7.11s lap; sim: 80% fewer collisions; M=1024 x N=300 = 3.07e5 rollouts/step on RTX3090 at 44.3 Hz

claims.claim: Tail-compression of the rollout-cost distribution before the softmax is sufficient for robustness gains; but the CVaR route needs ~300x extra rollouts per candidate, which is categorically infeasible at K<=256 CPU. FPL's bounded [0,1] atoms compress tails for free, making FPL a zero-cost surrogate for this weight-side mechanism — the closest alternative explanation for the in-repo FPL robustness win.
claims.quantitative: 300 auxiliary rollouts per candidate trajectory

claims.claim: STL robustness can be used inside a path-integral optimizer with NO smoothing: the non-differentiable min/max robustness is evaluated exactly on each sampled trajectory and added as terminal cost, with a variance-shrinking (beta->0) schedule providing convergence — sampling sidesteps the vanishing-gradient problem that plagues gradient/CBF methods on logic costs. This is prior art for logic-structured costs in path-integral control, but it is deterministic offline trajectory planning, not receding-horizon MPC.
claims.quantitative: Problem II: PI 0.12s vs GRAD 1.27s, MIP 1.16s, CMA-ES 1.62s; Problem III: PI 25.07s vs CMA-ES 79.82s, others >3600s timeout; M=955-81,650 samples, J=19-75 shrink phases, CPU (Ryzen 5)
claims.setting: Offline planning: integrator, 4D motion planning, single-track vehicle with 5 obstacles, K=10-50 steps
claims.where: Eq. for terminal cost E~(x_K); benchmark tables Problems I-III

claims.claim: STL-SVPIO claims plain MPPI fails on sparse long-horizon logic costs (probability of sampling a valid sequence decays exponentially with horizon) and fixes it interaction-side: LogSumExp-smoothed STL robustness gradients transport 10 mutually-repulsive Stein particles, beating MPPI robustness 0.108 vs 0.005 on reach-avoid.
claims.quantitative: Reach-avoid: SVPIO 0.108 robustness in 19.15ms/20 iters vs MPPI 0.005 in 187ms/200 iters; Franka/Half-Cheetah runs need 300 iterations, 593-635s total on RTX A6000
claims.setting: MuJoCo MJX (differentiable sim, GPU), navigation up to 600-step horizons, multi-agent, 7-DoF Franka, Half-Cheetah backflip
claims.where: Table I; Sec. on curse of dimensionality claim

claims.claim: The method requires differentiable-simulator gradients and offline runtimes of minutes — it is not a real-time controller and is incompatible with the CPU-MuJoCo no-gradient stack, so it threatens FPL novelty (logic-shaped path-integral costs) but not FPL's real-time closed-loop niche.
claims.quantitative: 593-635s for 300 iterations on GPU

objective_representation: logic (smoothed STL robustness as differentiable reward shaping)

claims.claim: Biased-MPPI injects ancillary-controller rollouts (LQR, energy-based, braking, go-to-goal, learned predictors) as the first J of K samples; the re-derivation for arbitrary sampling distributions cancels the usual importance-sampling cross-terms, so weights simplify to pure exp(-S/lambda). At K=50 it achieved 0 collisions where vanilla MPPI had 4-7 even at K=2000 — a proposal-side mechanism that succeeds by injecting external structure rather than adapting noise statistics, i.e., outside the failed in-repo family.
claims.quantitative: Two-vessel: 0 vs 4 collisions (K=50), 0 vs 7 (K=2000); Herengracht: 50/50 vs 45/50 success (K=1000); real Jackal: 0 vs 6 collisions; 10-50 Hz, horizon 50 steps
claims.setting: IEEE RA-L; pendulum, vessel navigation, real Clearpath Jackal; K=50-2000, CPU-scale budgets
claims.where: Eq. 9 sample construction, simplified weight equation, vessel/robot result tables

claims.claim: The mechanism transfers directly to FPL: per-fulfillment-atom greedy or classical controllers could be injected as biased samples with exact weights, carrying FPL structure into the proposal without touching covariance — an untried, CPU-free idea for the repo.

Predictive Sampling — nominal spline + N-1 Gaussian perturbations, take the best — is competitive with iLQG and CEM at N=10 rollouts on humanoid standing, quadruped terrain/recovery, and Shadow-Hand cube reorientation, with 1-20 ms planning updates on CPU. Sampler sophistication matters far less than spline action parameterization and cost design.
claims.quantitative: N=10 rollouts all tasks; sigma 0.1-0.25; horizons 23-35; 1-20ms/update; humanoid simulates 4000x realtime on one CPU thread
claims.setting: MJPC, CPU only (72-core Xeon and M1 Pro laptop), MuJoCo; replicated pattern (tiny-K spline sampling across morphologies) independently confirmed by arxiv:2409.10469 and arxiv:2511.19204
claims.where: Table 1 planner settings; Sec. 3 algorithm; Sec. 4 tasks

claims.claim: MJPC costs are sums of weighted norms of residuals with an optional risk-sensitive exponential transform c=(e^{Rl}-1)/R — the canonical hand-tuned linear/weighted-norm representation FPL competes against, with risk transform as the only built-in nonlinearity.
claims.quantitative: Humanoid: M=6 terms, weights 100/1/100/10/0.01/0.025
claims.where: Cost function section (norms, risk parameter R)

objective_representation: linear weighted norms with optional risk transform

claims.claim: Reference-free sampling MPC with cubic Hermite splines over position AND velocity control points plus diffusion-inspired noise annealing discovers emergent gaits (trot, gallop 2.0 m/s, jump 0.68m, backflip, handstand) on a real Go2 and a 37-DoF G1 humanoid with only 30 samples (quadruped) / 60-70 (humanoid) at 50 Hz on a Mac Studio CPU — a direct one-controller-across-morphologies competitor at the same compute class as the repo.
claims.quantitative: 30 samples quadruped, 60-70 humanoid; 50 Hz, 20-30ms/update, 3 iterations; jump 68.4+/-0.2 cm; walking 10/10, handstand 10/10
claims.setting: Real Unitree Go2 + simulated G1 humanoid, CPU (M3), no GPU
claims.where: Sec. on Hermite parameterization; results and ablation tables

claims.claim: RMPPI provides the principal formal robustness alternative to FPL: an augmented importance sampler over coupled nominal+real systems with an embedded tracking controller (iLQG/CCM), plus a proven free-energy growth bound as a function of constraint satisfaction, tracking convergence rate, and sampling error. Architecture-side (planner-tracker interaction), not cost-side.
claims.quantitative: Bound: ΔF <= (alpha - F(x0*)) + 2*EMV + (L_phi*gamma^T + L_q(1-gamma^T)/(1-gamma))*D_F
claims.setting: IEEE RA-L 2021; simulation + real GT AutoRally, GPU sampling

claims.claim: On real hardware the robustness machinery bought almost no headline performance: lap times statistically indistinguishable (RMPPI 31.07+/-0.33s vs MPPI 30.67+/-0.53s); the benefit is tolerating higher slip (0.84 vs 0.63 rad) without crashing. Formal-guarantee robustness delivers marginal empirical gains over plain MPPI in-distribution, supporting the 'good-enough plain MPPI + better cost' framing of H-A.

RC-MPPI shows model-plant mismatch perturbs MPPI importance weights in proportion to residual magnitude and inversely with temperature, and adapts three coupled knobs online from prediction-execution residuals (raise temperature, tighten constraints, contract exploration) — a schedule-side mismatch mechanism competing with H-A's claim that one fixed FPL spec suffices, but validated only on an LTI point mass and planar 2R arm.
claims.quantitative: No headline numbers in accessible text; probabilistic constraint-violation bounds under Lipschitz dynamics

claims.claim: The PI-MPC survey organizes the field around 'optimal distribution = Boltzmann weight x prior' with design axes of variational family (Gaussian/GMM/particles), prior/proposal, divergence (forward vs reverse KL), and temperature — and explicitly notes the Boltzmann exp(-J/lambda) form has 'no strict theoretical requirement' and alternatives are possible, legitimizing FPL's S=-log(u) transform as a valid weight-side design choice.

The survey contains NO discussion of temporal-logic, bounded, or otherwise structured cost languages, and lists cost/sample-complexity theory and decision-delay as open problems — the cost-representation axis FPL occupies is absent from the field's own map, supporting FPL's novelty positioning.
claims.where: Open problems section; absence check across survey

objective_representation: other (survey; treats cost as arbitrary J)

claims.claim: Whole-body MPPI on a real Unitree Go1 works with 30 samples at 100 Hz on a desktop CPU by sampling 4 cubic-spline control points in joint space (0.4s horizon, T=40): walking, climbing a 0.24m box, and box pushing (9/10 forward) — the first real-world whole-body sampling-MPC deployment on legged hardware, directly at the repo's compute class.
claims.quantitative: 30 samples, 100 Hz, T=40 (0.4s), i9-12900KS CPU; box push 9/10 forward, 6/10 angled; optimal lambda~0.1
claims.setting: Real Unitree Go1, MuJoCo parallel rollouts, CPU

claims.claim: Ablations found cubic splines beat direct/zeroth-order sampling, performance plateaus at ~100 Hz replanning, and 40-50-step horizons are best — proposal parameterization and replan rate, not sampler cleverness, are the effective levers; costs are plain weighted quadratic/L1 tracking terms.
claims.quantitative: Spline > direct sampling in all ablations; lambda=0.1

claims.claim: Tsallis VI-MPC proves the cost-to-weight transform is a free design axis: the deformed exponential exp_r(-J/lambda) = (1 - J/gamma)_+^{1/(r-1)} interpolates continuously between MPPI (r->1, exponential) and CEM (r->inf, hard threshold), with an explicit absolute-risk-aversion coefficient A(J) = -(r-2)/((r-1)(gamma-J)). Since MPPI-with-FPL computes exp(-S/lambda) = u^{1/lambda} with u a bounded power-mean, FPL is formally a member of this weight-transform family — power-law weighting on bounded fulfillment.
claims.quantitative: Special cases: r->1 MPPI, r->inf CEM step function

claims.claim: Empirically the Tsallis transform mainly reduces variance and helps most in high dimensions: planar navigation -4.4% mean cost but -84% std vs MPPI; humanoid (56D state) mean improved 112% with -66% std — evidence that reshaping the weight transform alone yields robustness/consistency gains that grow with morphology complexity, consistent with the in-repo FPL result pattern.
claims.quantitative: Planar: 28714 vs 30023 mean, 570 vs 3644 std; humanoid: -899.27 vs -423.79 mean, 80 vs 234 std; N=256-1024 samples, T=20-150
claims.setting: Isaac Gym GPU sims: planar nav, quadcopter, Franka, Ant, 56D humanoid; Gaussian/GMM/Stein policies

objective_representation: risk (deformed-exponential weight transform over standard costs)
